business: The Aldera: magnesium in single-serve capsule sachets (pure bisglycinate and a 3-form complex)
by_segment: Urban professional woman with a busy day outside home
why_not: NONE. The first thing I noticed was $29.99 for 30 sachets, which is double what I pay for my 8-form complex in a flash sale, and the 3-form Complex has fewer forms than what I already take. I take magnesium at night at home, so a pocket sachet solves a problem I barely have, even with the nights at my partner's.

NONE. What I noticed first was $29.99 and 2 capsules in every sachet. I hate swallowing pills, and two a day is already more than I want. I paid about half that for a bottle of 8 forms of magnesium in a flash sale and it lasted me 3 months, and this box is gone in 30 days.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was 'Every batch lab-tested' with the QR code, which is nice, but I already take magnesium at night at home and I have a drawer full of half-used bottles. I don't need a sachet to go.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was the QR code and the 'Every batch lab-tested' line, which is more proof than most brands give, but I already take magnesium at night at home, so a pocket sachet solves a problem I do not have. why_yes: PURE. The first thing I noticed was the sachets: one a day, tear it open with one hand, toss it in my bag, and I'm out the door all day anyway. I've watched a bunch of glycinate-for-sleep videos, so I'd try one box, but $29.99 still feels like double what I paid for my big bottle.

PURE. First thing I noticed was the sachets: one tear, pocket-sized, so I can toss one in my bag and take it at my partner's place instead of hauling a bottle around. $29.99 for 30 days with free shipping works out to about $1 a day, and the batch QR is a nice touch, so I'd try one box.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was 'no magnesium oxide' and the QR lab report, because citrate wrecks my stomach and the Complex has citrate in it, so I would skip that one. A dollar a day for the glycinate with free shipping is okay, and I would try one box, but I would rather catch it on a flash sale or coupon.

PURE. The first thing I saw was "200 mg, no magnesium oxide" and the QR batch report from a named ISO 17025 lab, which is exactly what I check before buying. A dollar a day is fine, and a sachet in my gym bag works better than a bottle I forget on the counter.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was "Every batch lab-tested" with the QR on the box, and the fact that the Bisglycinate has no oxide. Citrate wrecks my stomach, so I skip the Complex, but a named lab report I can open is the only proof I would accept from a supplement, so I would try one box.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was the QR on the sachet and the "Every batch lab-tested" line, which is rare for TikTok Shop supplements. At about $1 a day with free shipping I would try one box of the single bisglycinate, but only if it is on a flash sale or has a coupon.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was "magnesium bisglycinate" and the single-serve sachets, because that is exactly the glycinate everyone in my feed keeps saying helps sleep, and a sachet fits in my work bag. $29.99 is a little steep for a month, but I would grab one box on impulse to try it.

PURE. First thing I noticed was 'Magnesium, 200 mg' and 'no magnesium oxide' on the box, and the bisglycinate is the one all those sleep videos kept talking about, so I'd grab one box on impulse. I'd skip the Complex because it has citrate and citrate wrecks my stomach.
